subject: English
title: Research and Informative Writing Unit — Y7 English
tool_context: Research and informative writing unit — students investigate a topic using multiple sources, evaluate and synthesise information, and produce an informative or persuasive text (explanation, report, or argument). The unit activates Literacy analysing and creating strands as the primary sequence, with Language concept standards (text structure, cohesion, vocabulary) activated as writing tools. LY01 (technology and texts) grounds the unit in contemporary research contexts.
progression_endpoint: Students produce a structured informative or persuasive text on a researched topic that selects and organises ideas using appropriate text structures and idea structures, uses specialist vocabulary accurately, and substantiates claims with evidence synthesised from multiple sources.

phases.label: Investigating
phases.checkpoint: Students can locate and read texts on their research topic from multiple sources, explain how technology shapes how those texts are encountered, and identify specialist vocabulary relevant to the topic — they are ready to move from locating information to analysing and evaluating it.

waypoints.note: Establishing how digital technologies shape the research process — search algorithms, source types, and how texts are encountered online vs in print.
Identifying specialist and technical vocabulary in research sources — building the vocabulary needed to read and write about the topic.
Inferencing while reading sources — what is the source assuming the reader already knows, and what gaps does the reader need to fill?
Identifying terms with both everyday and technical meanings in the topic area — building precision before writing begins.
Examining how technology shapes the texts produced on this topic — what forms (articles, videos, infographics) are available and what each enables.

phases.label: Analysing and Synthesising
phases.checkpoint: Students can analyse how language features shape meaning in their sources, identify and explain the idea structures used, and summarise key ideas across multiple sources — they have the synthesised content needed to plan and draft their own text.

waypoints.note: Analysing how language features in research sources shape meaning — which sources are most reliable and why, based on language choices.
Identifying idea structures in sources — is this source organised by taxonomy, cause-effect, or chronology? How does that serve its purpose?
Summarising key ideas across sources — determining what is essential from each source and how the ideas relate to each other.
Analysing how the same topic is represented differently across sources for different audiences — what varies and why.
Selecting the idea structure for their own text — choosing cause-effect, taxonomy or chronology based on the topic and purpose of the text they will write.

phases.label: Drafting
phases.checkpoint: Students can produce a structured draft informative or persuasive text that organises synthesised information using an appropriate text structure and idea structure, uses specialist vocabulary accurately, and guides the reader with cohesion devices.

waypoints.note: Identifying the purpose of the text being written and selecting the appropriate text structure — explanation, report, or argument.
Selecting language features appropriate to the text type and audience — register, vocabulary, sentence complexity.
Using topic sentences and paragraph structure to guide the reader through the draft.
Planning the informative or persuasive text — mapping the idea structure, structural stages and language choices before drafting.
Using overviews, initial and concluding paragraphs as cohesion devices in the draft.
Creating and editing the draft — making deliberate structural and language choices and editing for meaning.

phases.label: Publishing
phases.checkpoint: Students can publish a structured informative or persuasive text or present their research in a spoken or multimodal format, with deliberate structural and language choices that serve the purpose and audience — the text demonstrates the integrated research, analytical and writing capabilities developed across the unit.

waypoints.note: Final editing — reviewing text structure, cohesion, vocabulary precision and language feature choices.
Planning a spoken or multimodal presentation of research findings — an alternative or complementary publishing mode.
Delivering the presentation — selecting voice features and visual elements that serve the informative or persuasive purpose.
